reading.why: 这段覆盖今天全部 10 个词。读的时候别查字典——先猜，读完再回头看词表，你会发现它们在句子里有了位置。

speaking.q: Describe an important decision you made. You should say: what the decision was; when you made it; what alternatives you had; and explain why you think it was important.
speaking.ans:
The decision I'd describe is deciding to leave a stable job without having another one lined up. That was about a year ago.

At the time the choice looked different from how it looks now. On paper I had two options: stay, keep the salary and the title, and wait for a better moment to move; or leave and figure out the next thing while looking. The reasonable choice was obviously the first one. Almost everyone I trusted said so, and they weren't being unkind — they were right about the risk.

What made me leave was a realisation that was not really about the job. I noticed that I'd been choosing the second-best version of a career I wasn't sure I wanted. Staying would have been comfortable and it would have made the next decision harder, not easier, because every year the salary gets a bit better and the switching cost gets a bit higher.

Was it a good decision? I don't think I'm the right person to judge yet, honestly. What I can say is that it forced me to find out what I'm actually good at, rather than what I've done before. That's worth something even if the timing turns out to have been bad.
speaking.note: 「我不知道这决定好不好」这种诚实比「这是我最正确的决定」高级得多。注意「choosing the second-best version of a career」是全文最强的一句。
speaking.swap: 换成你真实的决定。保留「承认风险、不确定结论」的态度——考官更信这个。

speaking.q: What do you usually do at weekends?
speaking.ans: It depends on how the week went. If I've been staring at a screen for five days, I try to spend Saturday somewhere with no signal — a long walk, or a book in a café where nobody knows me. Sunday is more practical: I plan the week, catch up on the reading I skipped, and try not to panic about Monday.
speaking.note: 「It depends」开头很好，避免变成一个贫乏的清单。「where nobody knows me」这种细节很生动。
speaking.swap: 换成你真实的周末节奏。保留「周六恢复 / 周日准备」这个对照结构。

speaking.q: Do you prefer reading paper books or e-books?
speaking.ans: Paper, though not for the reason people usually give. I don't think paper is inherently more romantic — it's that I can't skim a physical book convincingly. On a screen I scroll and convince myself I've read the page. With paper, my eye has to travel across every line, so I actually finish what I start.
speaking.note: 不要重复「纸质书有味道」这种陈词。给一个功能性理由（物理限制导致真读完了）更有说服力。
speaking.swap: 如果你确实更爱电子书，就说它的理由：搜索、随身、便宜。关键是给出「别人没想到的理由」。

posts.wordtips: 今天这 10 个词里，优先掌握出现频率最高的那三四个；其余的先做到「见到能认出来」，写作时自然会用上。

posts.title: 教育与学习 · 为什么我重新开始学英语

reading.why: 教育类是雅思写作和口语 Part 3 的第一大话题。今天这段覆盖 10 个核心词，读完请用中文说出「死记硬背 vs 批判性思维」这对矛盾。

speaking.q: Do you enjoy learning languages?
speaking.ans: I do now, though I didn't when I was younger. At school, English was just another subject I had to pass — I memorised vocabulary lists and forgot them within a week. Things changed when I started reading music criticism in English. I wanted to understand why a reviewer called an album 'deceptively simple', and that curiosity did what ten years of exams couldn't. So now I'd say I learn languages out of appetite rather than obligation.
speaking.note: 结构：现在的答案 → 转折 → 一个具体的触发点。考官最想听「一个具体细节」，不是「英语很重要」。
speaking.swap: 把 reading music criticism 换成你自己真实的触发点：看美剧、和一个外国朋友聊天、读论文、听播客。

speaking.q: Do you think it's important to learn a second language?
speaking.ans: I think it changes what you can access rather than simply adding a skill. My work involves a lot of reading about AI products, and the best material is still published in English first — by the time something is translated, the conversation has moved on. Beyond that, there's a subtler benefit: when you speak a language badly but willingly, you get used to being wrong in public, and that turns out to be useful in almost every other part of life.
speaking.note: 两个层次：实用层（获取信息）+ 心理层（容忍犯错）。第二层是 7 分以上的加分点。
speaking.swap: 把 AI products 换成你的行业；「being wrong in public」这个观察很通用，可以保留。

speaking.q: Describe a subject you found difficult but now find interesting. You should say: what the subject was; when you studied it; why it was difficult; and explain why your attitude changed.
speaking.ans:
I'd like to talk about statistics. I first met it during my master's degree in finance, and I have to admit I struggled badly. The formulas themselves weren't the problem — I could follow the algebra. What defeated me was that I couldn't see what any of it was for. We were asked to compute confidence intervals for abstract datasets, and I remember thinking that this had nothing to do with anything I cared about.

It was difficult for a second reason, which is less flattering. I'd been good at exams my whole life by being good at memorising, and statistics doesn't reward that. You can memorise the formula and still get the interpretation wrong. It exposed a habit I'd been relying on for years.

My attitude changed quite suddenly, when I started working on real data. I was asked to judge whether a difference in survey results between two regions was meaningful or just noise, and I realised I finally had a reason to care. Once the question was concrete, the statistics stopped being abstract machinery and became the only honest way to answer it. Now I find it genuinely elegant — it's a discipline for admitting how little you can actually conclude, which is rarer and more valuable than it sounds.
speaking.note: Part 2 拿高分的关键是「讲一个变化」而不是「描述一个科目」。注意用了两层困难 + 一个转折点 + 一个现在的评价。全程约 2 分钟。
speaking.swap: 如果你不想讲统计，可换成：编程 / 会计 / 数据可视化。把「我喜欢记忆式学习」这个自我观察保留，它让你显得真实。

posts.wordtips: 今天 10 个词里，最值得直接用在作文的是 critical thinking、vocational training、academic performance。rote learning 和 peer pressure 是「负面词」，写议论文时用来描述问题很顺手。

words.ex: Historians believe the ancient letters were sealed with wax to protect their contents.

words.ex: Few crops can survive in such an arid climate, where rainfall is extremely rare.

words.ex: Replacing traditional light bulbs with energy-saving ones can greatly reduce electricity consumption.
words.zh: 用节能灯泡替换传统灯泡可以大大降低电力消耗。

defs: 蜂房巢室；细胞；单人牢房
n. 细胞; 单人房间; 基层组织
words.ex: The honeycomb is made up of thousands of hexagonal cells built by worker bees.
words.zh: 蜂巢由工蜂建造的成千上万个六边形巢室组成。

words.ex: Students must cite all sources properly, or their essays may be rejected for plagiarism.
words.zh: 学生必须正确引用所有资料来源，否则论文可能因抄袭而被拒。

reading.en: In many **arid** regions, agricultural innovation has become a vital **axis** of sustainable development, since conventional farming often struggles where rainfall is scarce. One promising approach involves cultivating crops beneath a protective layer of **wax**, which significantly reduces water loss from the soil surface. Researchers also **cite** traditional practices, such as using **bark** mulch, as evidence that local knowledge can complement modern techniques. Meanwhile, engineers have redesigned the **barn** so that its roof **brim** channels rare rainwater into storage tanks, and a single solar **bulb** now lights the interior at night. Each storage **cell** within these tanks preserves every precious drop, while the **tag** of “climate-smart farming” has helped attract international funding. Although critics sometimes **bark** that such projects are too costly, pilot studies suggest they raise yields substantially. Consequently, this integrated model deserves serious consideration wherever drought threatens food security.
reading.zh: 在许多**干旱**地区，农业创新已成为可持续发展的关键**轴心**，因为传统耕作在降雨稀少的地方往往举步维艰。一种前景可观的方法是在一层保护性**蜡**下种植作物，这能显著减少土壤表面的水分流失。研究人员还**引用**诸如使用**树皮**覆盖物等传统做法，作为本地知识能够补充现代技术的证据。与此同时，工程师重新设计了**谷仓**，使其屋顶**边缘**将稀少的雨水引入储水箱，而一盏太阳能**灯泡**如今在夜间照亮内部。这些水箱中的每个储水**单元**都保存着每一滴珍贵的水，而“气候智能型农业”的**称号**也帮助吸引了国际资金。尽管批评者有时会**大声抱怨**此类项目成本过高，但试点研究表明它们能大幅提高产量。因此，在干旱威胁粮食安全的任何地方，这一综合模式都值得认真考虑。
reading.why: 这段把你今天的 10 个词全串起来了。读第一遍别查词——先按上下文猜；读完再看上面的词表，你会发现这些词在句子里各自有了位置。

speaking.q: Do you prefer to spend time with a large group or a few close friends?
speaking.ans: A few, definitely. I'm not shy exactly, but I find large groups exhausting in a way I can't fully explain — I come home feeling like I've been performing rather than talking. With two or three people I can be slower and more honest, and I've noticed that's when I actually remember the conversation afterwards.
speaking.note: 「performing rather than talking」是很精准的对比。用「我记得那次对话」作为证据，比空说「我更放松」有说服力。
speaking.swap: 如果你更爱大群体，就说它的好处：能量、随机性、认识新人。保持「用具体体验作证据」的结构。

speaking.q: Should old traditions be preserved?
speaking.ans:
I'd want to distinguish preserving a tradition from preserving the practice of it, because those often conflict.

There's a strong case for keeping the knowledge. If a craft or a form of music disappears, you lose something you can't reconstruct from a description — the technique lives in people, not in documents. In that sense preservation is genuinely urgent.

The weaker case is the one that gets made most often, which is that a tradition should continue simply because it's old. Age isn't an argument; plenty of old things were bad ideas. And there's a real cost to this framing, because it tends to freeze practices that were always changing, turning something living into a museum piece.

So I'd say: preserve the knowledge, be sceptical of the obligation. The traditions that survive are usually the ones people keep choosing, not the ones they're told to keep.
speaking.note: 「preserve the knowledge vs preserve the obligation」这个拆分是全篇骨架。最后一句「活下来的是人们仍在选择的东西」很有力。
speaking.swap: 这类「应该保留 X 吗」的题，核心动作是「把 X 拆成两种东西」，然后分别判断。

speaking.q: Do you work or are you a student?
speaking.ans: I'm working, though the honest description is that I'm between two things. My background is in finance — I did a master's in that — but for the past year or so I've been working on AI products, which is a fairly big jump. Right now I'm taking some time to prepare for the next step, which involves both studying and job hunting.
speaking.note: 「between two things」比直接说「我在找工作」体面且真实。主动说出转折，反而让后面的话题有抓手。
speaking.swap: 把 finance→AI 换成你自己的转折。核心句式：My background is X, but recently I've been Y.

words.ex: Ancient potters shaped clay into bowls and left them to dry in the sun.

defs: n. 圆锥体,球果vt. 使成锥形
words.ex: The volcano's perfect cone shape attracts thousands of tourists to the island each year.
words.zh: 这座火山完美的锥形每年吸引成千上万的游客来到该岛。

defs: 把...塞进；（为应考）临时死记硬背
vt. 塞满,填满,猛吃vi. 贪吃n. 塞满
v.（超限）填塞，塞满；临时抱佛脚，为考试而学习
words.ex: Many students cram all night before exams instead of reviewing material gradually.
words.zh: 许多学生在考试前通宵死记硬背，而不是循序渐进地复习。

words.ex: The basement felt cold and damp, so we bought a machine to remove the moisture.
words.zh: 地下室又冷又潮湿，所以我们买了一台机器来除湿。

defs: 散发 (光、热、气等)；发出（声音）
words.ex: Older vehicles emit far more harmful gases than modern electric cars do.
words.zh: 老旧车辆排放的有害气体远远多于现代电动汽车。

n.叙事诗，史诗；a.英雄的；大规模的

words.zh: 这部电影是一部跨越两大洲三代人的史诗般的迁徙故事。

defs: n. 档案; 行列; v. 归档; 提出
words.ex: Please file these documents alphabetically so that they can be found quickly.
words.zh: 请按字母顺序把这些文件归档，以便快速查找。

defs: n. 缺点,裂纹,瑕疵,一阵狂风
words.ex: The main flaw in the study is that it ignores the influence of family background.
words.zh: 这项研究的主要缺陷是忽略了家庭背景的影响。

defs: 掷；快速翻转。随便的；宽泛的
vt. 掷,弹,轻击,空翻vi. 用指轻弹,抽打,蹦跳n. 抛,弹,筋斗
words.ex: The teacher asked students to flip the card over and read the question on the back.
words.zh: 老师让学生把卡片翻过来，读背面的问题。

reading.en: The shift toward digital learning archives has been celebrated as an **epic** advance in educational equity, yet a closer look reveals a troubling **flaw**: uneven access to reliable infrastructure. In many rural schools, students must **cram** into overcrowded rooms where the only computer is a battered laptop, and connectivity is as fragile as **damp** paper. Such conditions hardly **emit** the promise of modern pedagogy. Even worse, teachers rarely have time to **file** each learner's progress systematically, so valuable data simply vanish. To address this, policymakers should **flip** the current funding model and direct resources toward the most underserved districts rather than scattering them in an **even** but ineffective layer. A simple **clay** model of a **cone**, used in a hands-on science lesson, may teach more than a dozen disconnected tablets; meaningful investment, not technological theatre, is what genuine reform requires.
reading.zh: 向数字化学习档案的转变被誉为教育公平的一次**宏大**进步，然而细看之下却暴露出一个令人不安的**缺陷**：可靠基础设施的获取并不均衡。在许多乡村学校，学生不得不**挤**进拥挤的教室，唯一的电脑是一台破旧的笔记本电脑，网络连接像**潮湿**的纸张一样脆弱。这样的条件几乎无法**散发**现代教学法的希望。更糟的是，教师很少有时间系统地**归档**每个学习者的进步，因此宝贵的数据就这样消失了。为解决这一问题，政策制定者应当**翻转**当前的资助模式，把资源投向最缺乏服务的地区，而不是把它们分散成**均匀**却无效的一层。在动手科学课上使用一个简单的**黏土****圆锥**模型，或许比十几台互不相连的平板电脑教得更多；真正有意义的投入，而非技术作秀，才是真正改革所需要的。

speaking.q: Why are you learning English?
speaking.ans: Two reasons, and they're not equally noble. The practical one is that most of the material I need for work is published in English first — by the time a decent article gets translated, the conversation has moved on. The less practical reason is that I want to be able to read a novel without feeling like I'm doing homework. That's the goal I actually care about.
speaking.note: 「not equally noble」是很好的自我觉察式表达。把功利理由和私人理由并列，比只说一个更真实。
speaking.swap: 把 practical reason 换成你的真实需求（考试、工作、移民、追剧）。

speaking.q: What kind of weather do you like?
speaking.ans: Overcast, which people find strange. Bright sun makes me feel like I should be outside doing something useful; grey weather gives me permission to stay in and read. I spent a winter in a place where it dropped to minus twenty, and oddly that was the most comfortable I've been — the cold was so serious that nobody expected you to be productive.
speaking.note: 反直觉的偏好（喜欢阴天）立刻抓住注意。后面用真实经历做支撑。
speaking.swap: 换成你真实的天气偏好 + 一个支撑它的记忆。

speaking.q: Describe a skill you learned that took a long time. You should say: what the skill is; when you learned it; how you learned it; and explain why it took so long.
speaking.ans:
The skill I'd describe is writing clearly — not writing well, which is a different and much rarer thing, but writing in a way that doesn't waste the reader's time. I've been working on it for about four years and I'm still not done.

I started because I had to. My job involved writing analysis that other people had to act on, and I kept getting the same response: 'I'm not sure what you're telling me to do.' That was humbling. I thought I was being thorough. I was being long.

The way I learned was mostly by deleting. I'd write something, cut it in half, and see what survived. Then someone showed me that most of what I was cutting was the part where I explained that I wasn't sure. The uncertainty was real, but burying it in caveats made the whole document useless.

Why it takes so long is that the skill isn't grammatical — it's deciding what matters. You can learn grammar in months. Judging relevance takes years, because you have to be wrong in front of people a lot of times first. I'm better than I was. I still over-explain when I'm nervous.
speaking.note: 「writing clearly 不是 writing well」这个区分很好。最后一句「我紧张时还是会解释太多」收了漂亮的自知之明。
speaking.swap: 换成你真实的技能（开车、做饭、编曲、数据分析）。核心是「为什么它慢」要给一个认知层面的理由，不是「需要多练」。

reading.en: Environmental education can convey the **gist** of conservation, but it must be supported by robust science. Field studies show that when a **gale** tears through a valley, a sudden **hike** in temperature follows, disrupting the **gene** pool of fragile species. Microscopic threats such as each harmful **germ** spread faster under such stress. Meanwhile, a **herd** of deer may flee toward a **hawk** circling overhead, and hail can batter the **gear** that researchers rely on. To **gear** programs toward real solutions, teachers should **hail** local success stories and let students observe how water can **gush** from a restored spring. Such hands-on learning links abstract concepts to the living world, helping learners understand that protecting one species safeguards the entire ecosystem.
reading.zh: 环境教育可以传达保护工作的**主旨**，但必须得到可靠科学的支撑。实地研究表明，当**大风**席卷山谷时，气温会随之骤升，扰乱脆弱物种的**基因**库。在此类压力下，每一种有害**细菌**等微观威胁都会传播得更快。与此同时，一群**鹿**可能会朝头顶盘旋的**鹰**奔逃，而**冰雹**会砸坏研究人员依赖的**设备**。为了使课程**适应**真正的解决方案，教师应当**赞扬**当地的成功案例，并让学生观察水如何从修复后的泉眼中**涌出**。这种动手学习将抽象概念与鲜活的自然世界联系起来，帮助学习者理解：保护一个物种就是保护整个生态系统。

speaking.q: Is competition good for children?
speaking.ans:
It depends entirely on what the competition is about and who's watching, which is why I don't trust general answers.

Competition against a measurable standard can be extremely useful. It gives a child a clear signal about where they stand, and losing in that setting teaches something that praise cannot — that effort and outcome are correlated but not identical, which is an uncomfortable and necessary lesson.

What's damaging is competition for a limited number of positions, where winning requires someone else to lose. That structure teaches a very specific thing: that other people are obstacles. And it's often applied far too early, before a child has any way of separating 'I lost' from 'I am a loser'.

So my position would be that competition is a tool, and like most tools the question isn't whether it's good but whether it's being used at the right age for the right thing.
speaking.note: 「competition against a standard」vs「competition for positions」这个区分是关键。结尾用「工具」框架收口比给结论安全。
speaking.swap: 「X 对孩子好不好」类问题都可用：区分两种形态 → 各给判断 → 用「取决于用法」收口。

speaking.q: Do you like music?
speaking.ans: I do, and more than just listening — I write and record my own songs, so music takes up a strange amount of my thinking time. The odd thing is that the more I learn about how a track is made, the harder it becomes to listen casually. I notice the mixing decisions now. Sometimes I miss being able to just enjoy it.
speaking.note: 「the more...the harder...」这个结构在口语里很显水平。承认代价（失去纯粹听歌的乐趣）比单纯夸音乐好。
speaking.swap: 如果你不创作，可以换成「我听得很多，而且有偏好」+ 一个具体的歌手或专辑。

speaking.q: Where are you from?
speaking.ans: I'm from Shenyang, in the north-east, though I've moved around a lot since then — Beijing for university, then Zhuhai and Suzhou for work. Shenyang still feels like home in a way the other places don't. When people ask, I usually say I'm from the north, because the accent gives it away before I get a chance to explain.
speaking.note: 「一个细节胜过三个形容词」。最后那句「口音先说漏了」是自然的口语推理。
speaking.swap: 换成你的真实家乡 + 一句家乡特征。不要列城市清单，选一个能展开的细节。

reading.en: Urban ecosystems offer a revealing case of how nature adapts to human environments. In many cities, a single **hive** can thrive on rooftops, where bees forage within a dense **mode** of settlement that reshapes local ecology. Although such insects are often viewed as a nuisance, their role as pollinators outweighs their reputation as **prey** for spiders and birds. On the **mean**, urban colonies survive at rates comparable to rural ones, with activity reaching its **peak** in late spring. Interestingly, the **horn** of a grazing goat and the **pine** beside a park may seem unrelated to bees, yet both shape the habitat mosaic. Public attitudes matter too: when a local athlete becomes an **idol**, public interest in conservation often rises. During the mating season, each queen must find a **mate**, and a single **mint** plant can attract dozens of insects, much like coins from a **mint** draw collectors.
reading.zh: 城市生态系统为自然界如何适应人类环境提供了一个颇具启发性的案例。在许多城市中，单个**蜂房**可以在屋顶繁盛，蜜蜂在密集的**模式**中觅食，从而重塑当地生态。尽管这类昆虫常被视为滋扰，但它们作为传粉者的作用超过了其作为蜘蛛和鸟类**猎物**的名声。**平均**而言，城市蜂群的存活率与乡村相当，其活动在晚春达到**顶点**。有趣的是，放牧山羊的**角**和公园旁的**松树**似乎与蜜蜂无关，但二者都塑造着栖息地的镶嵌格局。公众态度也很重要：当本地运动员成为**偶像**时，公众对保护的兴趣往往上升。在交配季节，每只蜂后都必须找到**配偶**，而一株**薄荷**就能吸引数十只昆虫，就像**铸币厂**铸出的硬币吸引收藏者一样。

speaking.q: Do you work or are you a student?
speaking.ans: I'm working, though the honest description is that I'm between two things. My background is in finance — I did a master's in that — but for the past year or so I've been working on AI products, which is a fairly big jump. Right now I'm taking some time to prepare for the next step, which involves both studying and job hunting.
speaking.note: 「between two things」比直接说「我在找工作」体面且真实。主动说出转折，反而让后面的话题有抓手。
speaking.swap: 把 finance→AI 换成你自己的转折。核心句式：My background is X, but recently I've been Y.

speaking.q: Why do some people find it difficult to separate work from personal life?
speaking.ans:
I'd separate two causes that get conflated: structural and psychological.

Structurally, remote work dissolved the physical boundary that used to do the separating for us. Commuting was miserable, but it also marked the end of the day. Without it, the day simply doesn't end — it just continues with a different set of tasks.

Psychologically, there's something less sympathetic going on. For a lot of people, work has become the primary source of identity and recognition. If your sense of worth comes from being useful, then stopping isn't rest, it's a mild threat. And a company will rarely discourage that, because it benefits from it.

What I'd push back on is the framing of this as an individual discipline problem. Telling people to set boundaries is a bit like telling them to sleep more — true, unhelpful, and it puts the cost on the person rather than on the arrangement that created the problem.
speaking.note: 注意最后那段「把责任推给个人是偷懒」——这种对常见建议的批评很有力，是 Part 3 上 7.5 的标志。
speaking.swap: 任何「为什么有些人 X」的问题都可以套「结构原因 + 心理原因」两层。

speaking.q: Do you prefer to spend time with a large group or a few close friends?
speaking.ans: A few, definitely. I'm not shy exactly, but I find large groups exhausting in a way I can't fully explain — I come home feeling like I've been performing rather than talking. With two or three people I can be slower and more honest, and I've noticed that's when I actually remember the conversation afterwards.
speaking.note: 「performing rather than talking」是很精准的对比。用「我记得那次对话」作为证据，比空说「我更放松」有说服力。
speaking.swap: 如果你更爱大群体，就说它的好处：能量、随机性、认识新人。保持「用具体体验作证据」的结构。

speaking.q: Do you prefer reading paper books or e-books?
speaking.ans: Paper, though not for the reason people usually give. I don't think paper is inherently more romantic — it's that I can't skim a physical book convincingly. On a screen I scroll and convince myself I've read the page. With paper, my eye has to travel across every line, so I actually finish what I start.
speaking.note: 不要重复「纸质书有味道」这种陈词。给一个功能性理由（物理限制导致真读完了）更有说服力。
speaking.swap: 如果你确实更爱电子书，就说它的理由：搜索、随身、便宜。关键是给出「别人没想到的理由」。

speaking.q: Do you like music?
speaking.ans: I do, and more than just listening — I write and record my own songs, so music takes up a strange amount of my thinking time. The odd thing is that the more I learn about how a track is made, the harder it becomes to listen casually. I notice the mixing decisions now. Sometimes I miss being able to just enjoy it.
speaking.note: 「the more...the harder...」这个结构在口语里很显水平。承认代价（失去纯粹听歌的乐趣）比单纯夸音乐好。
speaking.swap: 如果你不创作，可以换成「我听得很多，而且有偏好」+ 一个具体的歌手或专辑。

speaking.q: Do you think money can buy happiness?
speaking.ans:
The research answer is that it can, up to a point, and then it stops — which is a more interesting finding than either extreme.

Below a certain level of income, money is basically buying the absence of stress: you can pay the bill, fix the thing, take the taxi. That's not a small effect; it's the difference between being able to think about your life and being unable to.

Above that level, what money buys is mostly optionality — the ability to say no. And I'd argue that's the genuinely valuable part, more than any purchase. The people I've known who seemed most at ease weren't spending more; they just had more room to refuse things.

What money can't buy is the part that actually determines whether a life feels good, which is roughly: whether you're doing something you chose, with people you'd choose again. That's not a satisfying answer at a dinner party, but I think it's the accurate one.
speaking.note: 「optionality — the ability to say no」是整段最亮的点。结尾「不是你买了什么，而是你能拒绝什么」很有分量。
speaking.swap: 这类「钱能不能买 X」的题，都用「分段讨论」：低区间解决什么 / 高区间解决什么 / 什么都解决不了的是什么。

reading.en: Music education offers a compelling case for broadening the school curriculum. When children join a **choir**, they must **adapt** their voices to a collective rhythm, a discipline that strengthens listening and cooperation. Teachers who **audit** rehearsals can identify pupils who need support, while carefully chosen repertoire may **amuse** reluctant learners and draw them into active participation. Schools should not **alter** this provision merely to satisfy narrow testing goals, nor should they **carve** music into an optional extra for the talented few. Just as a **crack** in a **crust** can weaken an entire structure, neglecting the arts may leave cognitive development fragile. A well-designed programme can **breed** confidence and persistence, and even modest classrooms can be **adorn**ed with student artwork to celebrate achievement, reminding us that a balanced education shapes the whole person.
reading.zh: 音乐教育为拓宽学校课程提供了有力例证。当孩子们加入**唱诗班**时，他们必须让自己的声音**适应**集体节奏，这种训练能增强倾听与合作能力。**旁听**排练的教师可以识别出需要支持的学生，而精心挑选的曲目则能**逗乐**不情愿的学习者，吸引他们积极参与。学校不应仅仅为了满足狭隘的考试目标而**改变**这一安排，也不应把音乐**雕刻**成少数有天赋者的可选附加项。正如**地壳**中的一道**裂缝**会削弱整个结构，忽视艺术可能使认知发展变得脆弱。设计良好的课程能够**培育**自信与坚持，甚至简陋的教室也可以用学生的艺术作品来**装饰**，以庆祝成就，提醒我们均衡的教育塑造的是完整的人。

speaking.q: Where are you from?
speaking.ans: I'm from Shenyang, in the north-east, though I've moved around a lot since then — Beijing for university, then Zhuhai and Suzhou for work. Shenyang still feels like home in a way the other places don't. When people ask, I usually say I'm from the north, because the accent gives it away before I get a chance to explain.
speaking.note: 「一个细节胜过三个形容词」。最后那句「口音先说漏了」是自然的口语推理。
speaking.swap: 换成你的真实家乡 + 一句家乡特征。不要列城市清单，选一个能展开的细节。

speaking.q: Describe something you own that is important to you. You should say: what it is; how long you've had it; how you got it; and explain why it's important.
speaking.ans:
I'd like to describe a fairly cheap pair of headphones, which sounds like an odd choice for something important.

I bought them about four years ago, in a period when I was moving cities every few months. They cost almost nothing. I got them in a hurry at an airport, because the pair I had broke the night before a flight.

What makes them matter is what happened after. I write music, and for a while those were the only headphones I had, so every song I finished in that period — three or four of them — was mixed on these. They're not good. They colour the sound badly, and I can hear it now that I have better ones. But that's precisely why they're important to me: they're the reason those tracks sound the way they do, in a technical sense I can't undo.

So it's not really the object I care about. It's that it's a physical record of a specific stretch of my life — a period when I had very little money and quite a lot of time, which is a combination I don't expect to have again.
speaking.note: 「便宜的东西却重要」这个反差是抓点。承认它的缺点（音质不好）+ 把缺点变成意义，是很好的结构。
speaking.swap: 换成你真实的物件。关键是找出「它的不完美恰恰是它重要的原因」这个角度。

speaking.q: Do you work or are you a student?
speaking.ans: I'm working, though the honest description is that I'm between two things. My background is in finance — I did a master's in that — but for the past year or so I've been working on AI products, which is a fairly big jump. Right now I'm taking some time to prepare for the next step, which involves both studying and job hunting.
speaking.note: 「between two things」比直接说「我在找工作」体面且真实。主动说出转折，反而让后面的话题有抓手。
speaking.swap: 把 finance→AI 换成你自己的转折。核心句式：My background is X, but recently I've been Y.

words.ex: The fertile soil of the river delta supports intensive agriculture and a dense human population.

defs: n. 草图，草稿; v. 起草; a. 供役使的
words.ex: The committee released a draft of the new environmental policy for public consultation last week.

defs: n. 排水; 消耗; v. (使)流走
words.ex: Excessive irrigation has drained the underground water reserves faster than they can be replenished.

defs: n. 精华,精锐,中坚分子

words.zh: 进入精英大学的机会仍然严重偏向来自富裕城市家庭的学生。

defs: 爆发；喷发；（斑疹等）突然出现
v.爆发；喷出(熔岩、水、气体、泥浆等)

defs: n. 群; 大量; v. 聚结

defs: n.(某地区或时代的)植物群
words.ex: The island's unique flora has evolved in isolation for millions of years, producing many endemic species.
words.zh: 该岛独特的植物群在隔离状态下进化了数百万年，产生了许多特有物种。

defs: n. 熔炉,铁工厂vt. 打制,锻炼,伪造vi. 锻造,伪造
words.ex: The two universities agreed to forge a partnership aimed at advancing research in renewable energy.
words.zh: 这两所大学同意建立合作伙伴关系，旨在推进可再生能源的研究。

defs: n. 标准度量,计量器vt. 精确计量,估计
n.标准规格(尤指宽度或厚度)；测量仪；v.测量
words.ex: It is difficult to gauge public opinion on the issue without conducting a large-scale survey.
words.zh: 如果不进行大规模调查，就很难判断公众对该问题的看法。

reading.en: Protecting a river **delta** requires more than an emotional appeal; it demands rigorous science and coordinated policy. Researchers first **draft** a management plan, then **gauge** sediment flow and water quality to judge whether the ecosystem is stable. If upstream dams **drain** the wetlands too quickly, native **flora** may collapse and fish stocks decline. A single engineering **fault**, such as poor irrigation design, can trigger conflict once nutrients **erupt** into algal blooms. Meanwhile, tourist **flocks** gather each summer, and an **elite** group of developers often pushes for hotels that damage the very landscape visitors admire. Local communities therefore **forge** new agreements that balance conservation with livelihoods, treating every weakness as a chance to improve governance rather than a reason to delay action.
reading.zh: 保护河流三角洲需要的不仅是情感呼吁，还需要严谨的科学与协调的政策。研究人员首先起草管理计划，然后测量泥沙流量和水质，以判断生态系统是否稳定。如果上游水坝过快排空湿地，本地植物群可能崩溃，鱼类资源也会下降。单一工程故障，例如灌溉设计不当，可能在营养物质爆发为藻华后引发冲突。与此同时，游客群每年夏天聚集，而一个精英开发商群体往往推动建设酒店，损害游客所欣赏的景观本身。因此，当地社区锻造新的协议，在保护与生计之间取得平衡，把每一个弱点视为改进治理的机会，而不是拖延行动的理由。

speaking.q: Do you think technology has improved education?
speaking.ans:
I'd say it has expanded access without necessarily improving learning, and those are different things.

The strongest argument for technology is distributional. A student in a small city can now watch lectures from people who would never have visited, and that's genuinely new. Twenty years ago that advantage was geographically locked.

But the case gets weaker when you ask about depth. Access to information isn't the bottleneck anymore — almost everyone I know has more material available than they can use. What's scarce is attention and a reason to care. And I'd argue technology has made both harder, not easier, because a screen is a place where distraction is always one tap away.

So my honest position is: technology solved the supply problem and left the demand problem untouched. Which means the next useful innovation in education probably isn't a better platform. It's something that makes people want to finish what they start.
speaking.note: 「solved the supply problem, left the demand problem untouched」是全篇核心。这个「分清两个问题」的动作在 Part 3 极其加分。
speaking.swap: 这套「它解决的是 A，不是 B」的框架适用于几乎所有「XX 有没有改善 YY」类问题。

speaking.q: Why are you learning English?
speaking.ans: Two reasons, and they're not equally noble. The practical one is that most of the material I need for work is published in English first — by the time a decent article gets translated, the conversation has moved on. The less practical reason is that I want to be able to read a novel without feeling like I'm doing homework. That's the goal I actually care about.
speaking.note: 「not equally noble」是很好的自我觉察式表达。把功利理由和私人理由并列，比只说一个更真实。
speaking.swap: 把 practical reason 换成你的真实需求（考试、工作、移民、追剧）。

speaking.q: Do you prefer reading paper books or e-books?
speaking.ans: Paper, though not for the reason people usually give. I don't think paper is inherently more romantic — it's that I can't skim a physical book convincingly. On a screen I scroll and convince myself I've read the page. With paper, my eye has to travel across every line, so I actually finish what I start.
speaking.note: 不要重复「纸质书有味道」这种陈词。给一个功能性理由（物理限制导致真读完了）更有说服力。
speaking.swap: 如果你确实更爱电子书，就说它的理由：搜索、随身、便宜。关键是给出「别人没想到的理由」。

posts.title: 文化 · 语言保护与生态隐喻

defs: n. 滑动,滑过,流水vi. 滑动,滑翔,溜走vt. 使滑动
words.ex: The eagle glided silently over the valley, scanning the ground for signs of prey.
words.zh: 老鹰无声地滑翔在山谷上空，扫视地面寻找猎物的踪迹。

defs: n.优美(尤指动作顺畅协调)
words.ex: The ballet dancer moved across the stage with remarkable grace, captivating the entire audience.
words.zh: 这位芭蕾舞者以非凡的优雅在舞台上移动，令全场观众着迷。

defs: v. 给予，授予; 同意; 承认; n. 拨款
words.ex: The government granted the research team a substantial fund to develop a new water purification system.
words.zh: 政府授予该研究团队一笔可观的资金，用于开发新的水净化系统。

defs: n. 孵化,舱口vt. 孵,孵出,策划vi. 孵化
words.ex: Sea turtles return to the same beach where they were born to lay eggs that will hatch weeks later.
words.zh: 海龟回到它们出生的同一片海滩产卵，这些卵将在几周后孵化。

defs: a. 潮湿的,湿润的,多湿气的
words.ex: The hot and humid climate of the tropical region makes it ideal for growing rice and tropical fruits.
words.zh: 热带地区湿热的气候使其非常适合种植水稻和热带水果。

defs: n. 习惯用语; (在艺术上所表现的)风格，特色
n.习语，语言的习惯用法；特色
words.ex: Learning idioms is essential for language learners who wish to understand everyday conversation among native speakers.
words.zh: 学习习语对于希望理解母语者日常对话的语言学习者来说至关重要。

defs: 无生气的；惰性的；不活泼
a. 惰性的,迟钝的,无活力的,呆滞的
words.ex: Noble gases are chemically inert, meaning they rarely react with other substances under normal conditions.
words.zh: 稀有气体在化学上是惰性的，这意味着它们在正常条件下很少与其他物质发生反应。

defs: vt. 推论出,推断vi. 作推论
words.ex: From the fossil evidence, scientists can infer that the species lived in a warm, humid environment.
words.zh: 从化石证据中，科学家可以推断该物种生活在温暖潮湿的环境中。

defs: 重要问题；发行。公布；发出
n. 发行,问题,后果,争端,出口vi. 发行,流出,传下,进行辩护,造成. . .
v.出来，流出；发给，分发；n.(书刊的)期
words.ex: Climate change is no longer a distant threat but an urgent issue requiring immediate global action.
words.zh: 气候变化不再是一个遥远的威胁，而是一个需要立即采取全球行动的紧迫问题。

words.ex: The international ban on ivory trade aims to protect elephants from being killed for their tusks.
words.zh: 国际象牙贸易禁令旨在保护大象免遭为获取象牙而被杀害。

reading.en: In discussions of language loss, scholars often **infer** from statistical trends that minority tongues will disappear within decades, yet such predictions risk overlooking the vitality that survives beneath apparently **inert** vocabularies. Consider the **idiom** embedded in everyday speech: a phrase may **glide** across generations with remarkable **grace**, carrying ecological knowledge that formal curricula rarely **grant** students. In **humid** tropical regions, for instance, farmers preserve terms describing how insects **hatch** after seasonal rains, a subtle vocabulary of timing that outsiders cannot easily decode. The central **issue** for educators is whether schools should treat such expressions as **ivory**-tower curiosities or as living evidence of community adaptation. When a language is reduced to a museum exhibit, its speakers lose the authority to name their own world; when it is nurtured, it becomes a tool for environmental resilience. Language policy, therefore, is never merely technical but deeply cultural.
reading.zh: 在讨论语言流失时，学者常从统计趋势**推断**少数族群语言将在数十年内消失，然而此类预测可能忽视看似**无生气的**词汇之下存续的活力。试看日常言语中的**习语**：一个短语可能以非凡的**优雅****掠过**代际，承载正规课程很少**授予**学生的生态知识。例如在**湿热的**热带地区，农民保留描述昆虫在季节性降雨后如何**孵化**的词语，这是一种外人难以解读的微妙时间词汇。对教育者而言，核心**重要问题**在于学校应将这些表达视为**象牙**塔中的奇珍，还是社区适应力的活证据。当一种语言被缩减为博物馆展品，其使用者便失去为自身世界命名的权利；当它得到培育，便成为环境韧性的工具。因此，语言政策从来不只是技术问题，而是深层的文化问题。

speaking.q: Describe a person who has influenced you. You should say: who this person is; how you know them; what they are like; and explain how they influenced you.
speaking.ans:
I'd like to talk about a former manager of mine — someone I worked with for less than a year, but who changed how I think about being wrong.

She was the head of a data team, and what struck me first was how comfortable she was saying 'I don't know' in a meeting with thirty people in it. I was twenty-four and terrified of exactly that. I assumed that admitting a gap would cost you authority. She seemed to gain it.

The specific moment I remember is a review where I'd presented an analysis I was quite proud of. She asked one question I couldn't answer, and instead of moving on she said, 'Let's not guess at that — can you find out by Thursday?' It wasn't a rebuke. It was almost worse, because it made me realise the standard wasn't 'look smart', it was 'be reliable'.

What she actually taught me wasn't a skill. It was that uncertainty is information, not failure. If you can say precisely where you don't know something, people trust the parts you do claim. I've used that in every project since — especially in AI work, where the honest answer is very often 'this looks plausible but I haven't verified it'.
speaking.note: Part 2 最容易变成流水账。这段的结构是：一句定性 → 一个反直觉观察 → 一个具体场景 → 一个提炼出的原则 → 落到现在。注意「It wasn't a rebuke. It was almost worse」这种转折。
speaking.swap: 换成你真实的某个人（老师、同事、朋友、家人）。保留结构：一句概括 → 一个具体的场景 → 一句你后来一直在用的话。

speaking.q: What do you usually do at weekends?
speaking.ans: It depends on how the week went. If I've been staring at a screen for five days, I try to spend Saturday somewhere with no signal — a long walk, or a book in a café where nobody knows me. Sunday is more practical: I plan the week, catch up on the reading I skipped, and try not to panic about Monday.
speaking.note: 「It depends」开头很好，避免变成一个贫乏的清单。「where nobody knows me」这种细节很生动。
speaking.swap: 换成你真实的周末节奏。保留「周六恢复 / 周日准备」这个对照结构。

defs: n. 抒情诗,歌词a. 抒情的
words.ex: The poet's early works are highly lyric, expressing deep personal emotions through vivid imagery.
words.zh: 这位诗人的早期作品极具抒情性，通过生动的意象表达深切的个人情感。

defs: v.戏弄性模仿；n.善于模仿他人言行的人
words.ex: Some birds can mimic human speech with surprising accuracy, which fascinates researchers studying animal cognition.
words.zh: 有些鸟类能以惊人的准确度模仿人类语言，这令研究动物认知的研究人员着迷。

words.ex: The oasis in the middle of the desert provides water and shade for travelers and local wildlife.
words.zh: 沙漠中央的绿洲为旅行者和当地野生动物提供水源和阴凉。

defs: 投；掷；球场；（棒球中的）投球
words.ex: The children pitched their tent near the lake and spent the evening watching the stars.
words.zh: 孩子们在湖边搭起了帐篷，傍晚时分观看星星。

defs: n. 枢轴,支点a. 枢轴的vi. 在枢轴上转动vt. 装枢轴于
n. 枢轴，中心；v. 旋转
words.ex: The discussion began to pivot around the question of who should bear the cost of environmental cleanup.
words.zh: 讨论开始围绕谁应承担环境清理费用这一问题展开。

defs: a. 平的; 简单的; 朴素的; n. 平原，草原
words.ex: Vast plains covered in grass stretch for hundreds of kilometers across the interior of the continent.
words.zh: 覆盖着草皮的广阔平原在大陆内陆延伸数百公里。

defs: 极地的；近极地的；对立的
words.ex: Polar ice caps are melting at an alarming rate due to rising global temperatures.
words.zh: 由于全球气温上升，极地冰盖正以惊人的速度融化。

defs: 新闻界；记者；报刊；出版社
n. 报刊，新闻界，通讯社; 挤压; v. 挤压; 催促
words.ex: The press played a crucial role in exposing the corruption scandal that led to the minister's resignation.
words.zh: 新闻界在揭露导致部长辞职的腐败丑闻中发挥了关键作用。

reading.en: Scientific exploration of the **lunar** surface has become a **pivot** for modern education, offering students a vivid case of how curiosity drives discovery. In **plain** language, researchers explain that any base near the **polar** regions must rely on local ice, turning a frozen site into a scientific **oasis** where life-support experiments can proceed. Students then **mimic** this logic in classroom projects, designing shelters from **linen**-like insulating fabrics and calculating the **pitch** of supply capsules dropped from orbit. Meanwhile, the **press** reports each mission, shaping public debate about funding priorities. A **lyric** essay assigned afterwards asks learners to reflect on humanity's place in space, linking technical facts with ethical questions. Such teaching does more than transmit knowledge; it trains young people to evaluate evidence, appreciate uncertainty, and communicate complex ideas clearly to society.
reading.zh: 对**月球**表面的科学探索已成为现代教育的**枢轴**，为学生提供了一个好奇心驱动发现的生动案例。用**简朴的**语言来说，研究人员解释说，**极地**地区附近的任何基地都必须依赖当地冰层，从而将一片冰封之地变成科学**绿洲**，使生命保障实验得以推进。随后，学生在课堂项目中**模仿**这一逻辑，用类似**亚麻布**的隔热织物设计庇护所，并计算从轨道投下的补给舱的**投掷**角度。与此同时，**新闻界**报道每一次任务，塑造关于资助优先事项的公众讨论。之后布置的一篇**抒情**散文要求学习者反思人类在太空中的位置，将技术事实与伦理问题联系起来。这种教学不仅传授知识，还培养年轻人评估证据、理解不确定性，并向社会清晰地传达复杂观点。

speaking.ans: Two reasons, and they're not equally noble. The practical one is that most of the material I need for work is published in English first — by the time a decent article gets translated, the conversation has moved on. The less practical reason is that I want to be able to read a novel without feeling like I'm doing homework. That's the goal I actually care about.

speaking.q: Describe an important decision you made. You should say: what the decision was; when you made it; what alternatives you had; and explain why you think it was important.
speaking.ans:
The decision I'd describe is deciding to leave a stable job without having another one lined up. That was about a year ago.

At the time the choice looked different from how it looks now. On paper I had two options: stay, keep the salary and the title, and wait for a better moment to move; or leave and figure out the next thing while looking. The reasonable choice was obviously the first one. Almost everyone I trusted said so, and they weren't being unkind — they were right about the risk.

What made me leave was a realisation that was not really about the job. I noticed that I'd been choosing the second-best version of a career I wasn't sure I wanted. Staying would have been comfortable and it would have made the next decision harder, not easier, because every year the salary gets a bit better and the switching cost gets a bit higher.

Was it a good decision? I don't think I'm the right person to judge yet, honestly. What I can say is that it forced me to find out what I'm actually good at, rather than what I've done before. That's worth something even if the timing turns out to have been bad.

On a screen I scroll and convince myself I've read the page. With paper, my eye has to travel across every line, so I actually finish what I start.

speaking.q: How will artificial intelligence change the kind of work people do?
speaking.ans:
I think the honest answer is that it will change work in ways that are easy to predict in aggregate and very hard to predict for any specific person — which is exactly why it's unsettling.

The predictable part is that tasks involving retrieval, formatting and first drafts are already being absorbed. That's not speculation; it's happening in my own work. What follows is that the value of a person shifts towards judgement — knowing which of five plausible outputs is actually right, and being accountable when it isn't.

The part I'm less sure about is whether that leaves enough work for everyone. The optimistic case is that it's like previous transitions and new categories of job appear. The pessimistic case is that this one moves faster than retraining cycles, so the adjustment cost lands on a specific generation rather than being spread out.

What I'd resist is both the utopian and the apocalyptic version. The realistic statement is: the technology is neither good nor bad, but the distribution of its benefits is a political question, not a technical one.

reading.en: The rapid expansion of social media has created a fertile environment for misinformation to **spawn** and spread across entire populations within hours. False claims often **swarm** through online platforms, overwhelming users before fact-checkers can respond, and this phenomenon can **spoil** public trust in legitimate journalism. The **trend** toward sensational content further complicates matters, as platforms reward engagement over accuracy, creating a **toxic** information ecosystem in which reasoned debate is increasingly difficult. Regulators face a **steep** challenge in curbing such harms without infringing free expression, and any attempt to **swamp** citizens with constant warnings risks desensitising them altogether. Moreover, every misleading story carries a hidden **thorn**: it can **sting** readers into reactive outrage rather than careful reflection. Consequently, media literacy education must become central to policy, equipping individuals to question sources critically and resist manipulation.
reading.zh: 社交媒体的迅速扩张为虚假信息创造了滋生的沃土，使其能在数小时内产生并传遍整个人群。虚假说法常常成群涌过网络平台，在事实核查人员作出回应之前就淹没用户，而这一现象会破坏公众对正当新闻业的信任。由于受众经常接触到被当作突发新闻重新包装的陈腐叙事，他们可能难以区分经核实的事实与谣言。追求耸动内容的趋势使问题更加复杂，因为平台奖励的是参与度而非准确性，从而形成有毒的信息生态，使理性辩论日益困难。监管者在遏制此类危害而不侵犯言论自由方面面临严峻挑战，而任何以持续警告淹没民众的尝试都可能使人们彻底麻木。此外，每一个误导性故事都带有隐藏的荆棘：它可能刺痛读者，使其作出冲动愤怒的反应而非审慎思考。因此，媒介素养教育必须成为政策的核心，使个人能够批判性地质疑信息来源并抵制操纵。

speaking.q: Should old traditions be preserved?
speaking.ans:
I'd want to distinguish preserving a tradition from preserving the practice of it, because those often conflict.

There's a strong case for keeping the knowledge. If a craft or a form of music disappears, you lose something you can't reconstruct from a description — the technique lives in people, not in documents. In that sense preservation is genuinely urgent.

The weaker case is the one that gets made most often, which is that a tradition should continue simply because it's old. Age isn't an argument; plenty of old things were bad ideas. And there's a real cost to this framing, because it tends to freeze practices that were always changing, turning something living into a museum piece.

So I'd say: preserve the knowledge, be sceptical of the obligation. The traditions that survive are usually the ones people keep choosing, not the ones they're told to keep.
speaking.note: 「preserve the knowledge vs preserve the obligation」这个拆分是全篇骨架。最后一句「活下来的是人们仍在选择的东西」很有力。
speaking.swap: 这类「应该保留 X 吗」的题，核心动作是「把 X 拆成两种东西」，然后分别判断。

speaking.ans: Overcast, which people find strange. Bright sun makes me feel like I should be outside doing something useful; grey weather gives me permission to stay in and read. I spent a winter in a place where it dropped to minus twenty, and oddly that was the most comfortable I've been — the cold was so serious that nobody expected you to be productive.

speaking.q: Describe a place you like to go to relax. You should say: where it is; how often you go there; what you do there; and explain why it helps you relax.
speaking.ans:
The place I'd describe isn't scenic. It's a particular stretch of riverside in Suzhou — maybe four hundred metres long, with a bench roughly in the middle that I've come to think of as mine.

I started going there about two years ago, during a period when work was going badly and I couldn't sleep. I'd walk there at ten or eleven at night. There were always a few other people — someone fishing who never caught anything, a couple arguing quietly. Nobody talked to me, which was the point.

What I did there was mostly nothing. Walked the same four hundred metres, sat on the bench, went home. But something in the repetition helped. When everything else was changing — job, city, plans — that stretch of river was exactly the same on a Tuesday as it had been in March.

I think that's why it works. It's not that the place is peaceful, exactly; it's that it's indifferent. It makes my problems feel smaller in a way that a sympathetic friend sometimes can't. I don't go as often now, but I still think of it as a place I could go.
speaking.note: 「不是景色美，是重复带来的稳定」这是高分点。最后一句「make my problems feel smaller」+「indifferent」是很成熟的表达。
speaking.swap: 换成你真实的地方（图书馆、健身房、某条街、某个咖啡馆）。保留「为什么它能让你放松」的功能性解释，而不是形容词堆砌。

speaking.q: Do you like music?
speaking.ans: I do, and more than just listening — I write and record my own songs, so music takes up a strange amount of my thinking time. The odd thing is that the more I learn about how a track is made, the harder it becomes to listen casually. I notice the mixing decisions now. Sometimes I miss being able to just enjoy it.
speaking.note: 「the more...the harder...」这个结构在口语里很显水平。承认代价（失去纯粹听歌的乐趣）比单纯夸音乐好。
speaking.swap: 如果你不创作，可以换成「我听得很多，而且有偏好」+ 一个具体的歌手或专辑。

speaking.q: Do you prefer to spend time with a large group or a few close friends?
speaking.ans: A few, definitely. I'm not shy exactly, but I find large groups exhausting in a way I can't fully explain — I come home feeling like I've been performing rather than talking. With two or three people I can be slower and more honest, and I've noticed that's when I actually remember the conversation afterwards.
speaking.note: 「performing rather than talking」是很精准的对比。用「我记得那次对话」作为证据，比空说「我更放松」有说服力。
speaking.swap: 如果你更爱大群体，就说它的好处：能量、随机性、认识新人。保持「用具体体验作证据」的结构。

reading.en: A university education should **attain** a balance between practical skills and intellectual curiosity, and the study of **botany** offers a clear illustration. Students who examine how plants survive on **barren** land learn to respect the fragile systems that sustain life, while a single **clause** in an environmental law can determine whether a habitat is protected or destroyed. This connection between science and policy deserves careful **debate**, since a **critic** of purely vocational training might argue that such knowledge carries genuine academic **credit**. Meanwhile, researchers studying the **cosmos** remind us that every **crater** on a distant planet tells a story of collision and survival, much like a **canvas** painted by nature itself. When students understand these links, they are better equipped to protect the world they inherit.
reading.zh: 大学教育应当在实用技能与求知欲之间**达到**平衡，而**植物学**的学习提供了一个清晰的例证。研究植物如何在**贫瘠**土地上生存的学生，会学会尊重维系生命的脆弱系统，而环境法中的一项**条款**就可能决定一个栖息地是被保护还是被摧毁。科学与政策之间的这种联系值得仔细**讨论**，因为一位**批评家**可能会指出，纯粹的职业培训所欠缺的正是这种知识所具有的真正学术**学分**价值。与此同时，研究**宇宙**的研究者提醒我们，遥远行星上的每一个**坑**都讲述着碰撞与生存的故事，就像大自然亲手绘制的一幅**油画布**。当学生理解这些联系时，他们就能更好地保护自己所继承的世界。

speaking.q: Do you prefer reading paper books or e-books?
speaking.ans: Paper, though not for the reason people usually give. I don't think paper is inherently more romantic — it's that I can't skim a physical book convincingly. On a screen I scroll and convince myself I've read the page. With paper, my eye has to travel across every line, so I actually finish what I start.
speaking.note: 不要重复「纸质书有味道」这种陈词。给一个功能性理由（物理限制导致真读完了）更有说服力。
speaking.swap: 如果你确实更爱电子书，就说它的理由：搜索、随身、便宜。关键是给出「别人没想到的理由」。

speaking.q: Is it better to live in a city or in the countryside?
speaking.ans:
I don't think the question has a general answer, and I'd be suspicious of anyone who gives one quickly.

What I can say is that the trade-off isn't the one people usually describe. The common framing is opportunity versus peace, and that's partly true. But the thing I noticed after living in six cities in five years is that cities don't actually give you more opportunities — they give you more options, which is not the same. Options cost attention. You spend a lot of energy deciding, and very little actually committing.

Smaller places have the opposite problem: fewer options means you commit to the ones you have, and that can be genuinely better for doing anything difficult. The catch is that they're much less forgiving if you turn out to be different from the people around you.

So I'd frame it as: cities are better if you're still deciding who you are; smaller places are better once you know. The mistake is optimising for the wrong stage.
speaking.note: 「more options ≠ more opportunities」这个区分是整段的价值所在。最后一句「优化错了阶段」是很漂亮的收尾。
speaking.swap: 这类「A 还是 B 更好」的题，最安全的答法就是「取决于阶段/取决于你是谁」，然后给出判据。
